title: Resetting the input head
statement: Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a\in\mathbb{N}$, and fix a schedule-alphabet input, a base configuration, an input-head position $p$, integer controller-head positions, and controller tapes. Starting in reset-start phase, after $\max(p,1)+1$ steps the machine is in copy-left phase with input head at position $1$; all controller tapes and their head positions, as well as the other configuration data, are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $W$ is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
a schedule-alphabet input and base configuration
replaced:
From a setup configuration in the reset-start phase with input head at an arbitrary
position $p \in \{0,\dots,|x|+1\}$, running exactly $\max(p,1)+1$ steps of the
oblivious schedule machine leads to the setup configuration in the copy-left phase with
input head at position $1$; all controller tapes and heads are unchanged.  (The reset
begins with a mandatory left move, so even the right blank boundary and the empty input
reach the left boundary before the final right move.)
